terra.problem: The claim that nobody is coming after God goes beyond His statement that He is the first and the last.
The business-card joke makes God's statement about Himself the target of humor.
The verse says the earth and heavens stand up together; it does not say nothing shakes or crumbles.
The comparison to unbroken cookies does not match the action of standing up together when summoned.
The verse asks which idol foretold these things; it does not describe the idols being present or remaining silent.
The verse does not describe an idol stepping up or a silent room. It asks which idol foretold these things.
The statement about Nineveh being a city in the Bible needs a reference outside this passage. Also, 'Wrong city' says the baker's answer is wrong.
The statement that Damascus is a city in the Bible needs a reference outside this passage.
The verse promises success for this chosen ally; it does not make a general statement that everyone the LORD brings gets the job done.
The promise that the ally will succeed does not establish that he never hesitates.
The joke about whispering behind the cooling racks makes the LORD's speaking the target of humor.
The ally acting against Babylon does not establish that a king of Babylon sending the unnamed speaker would be impossible.
'Wrong palace' calls the baker's answer wrong.
The imagined line about handing over the keys and saying good luck puts words in God's mouth.
The LORD says He directs people in the way they should go, not that He directs a road. The claim that a hidden road cannot be directed is also unsupported.
The explanation applies the waves image to the river. The verse compares peace to a river and righteousness to waves of the sea.
The explanation only rules out armies and repeats the verse. It feels generic rather than like Papa Dorin explaining the two images.
The explanation only repeats the verse and identifies the word name, without adding a natural explanation or Papa Dorin's personality.
The explanation only rules out the temple and repeats the verse. It feels generic.
The verse gives commands to leave and declare the news; it does not say they leave without sneaking or that they announce their departure.
The statement that Moses was Israel's leader needs a reference outside this passage.
